get.description: The user's own audit trail (logins, imports, exports, approvals, sends, deletions). Metadata only.
Aggregate counts only; admins never see user personal data.

put.description: Optional: a GitHub token only raises the API rate limit for public data. Stored encrypted; never returned or exported.

post.description: Step 1: store the file, detect encoding/delimiter/header, suggest a column mapping, preview rows.
Step 2: confirm mapping (+ required provenance for HR lists) and run the import in the background.

get.description: Diagnostics: every source row with its status and reasons (why was this rejected?).

post.description: Retention: delete the stored file and verbatim source values; derived contacts stay.
Only the user can verify this (e.g. they know the person still works there). We never infer 'verified'.

Candidates only (nothing is saved). A guessed token can belong to a different company with a similar name,
so each hit shows sample job titles and must be confirmed by the user.

Paste a job URL (read via schema.org JobPosting, robots respected) or the description itself.
Pasted text proves nothing about whether the role is open, so such jobs stay UNKNOWN until verified.

patch.description: Edits never change an existing version (approved or not); they create the next version.

post.description: Explicitly add an edited statement to your master profile as a confirmed fact, then re-validate as a new version.
Approving more than one message needs a confirmation that restates the count and the daily limit.

Starts the sender as a BACKGROUND task (pacing can take minutes, so it never runs inside a request). It sends only approved,
queued emails that pass every check, paces them, and never retries an ambiguous send. Poll /api/tasks/{id} for the result.
Creates follow-up DRAFTS that wait for your approval. Nothing is sent.
Sends ONE test email to your own address. The only place the app sends without a draft, and only ever to you.
